records.text: An orca inhabiting Northrend’s coastal waters.
Spirit healers describe a return to the realm of the living for a price, while cautioning that it may not yet be the traveler’s time. The return is presented as a choice.
A skunk found across Outland and Northrend.

Vice Admiral Keller commands Valgarde’s defense and treats holding the port as essential to the Alliance’s supply line into Northrend. He presses for help against the Dragonflayer attackers, rescue of captured townsfolk and scouts, and warnings to other threatened Alliance strongholds. The attack on his scouts has hardened his resolve. He also speaks of his wife and three children in Elwynn, giving his determination a personal stake.

Macalroy is wary of the green recruits sent by Fordragon to defend Valgarde, but judges an arriving traveler’s equipment and sees potential in them. With the port threatened and monsters overhead, he sends the traveler to Vice Admiral Keller to report and help shore up the defense.

Beltrand McSorf is an Explorers’ League archaeologist at Valgarde. After escaping an attack on his dig, he worries about his missing crew and seeks their recovered artifacts, beginning with Pulroy. Cryptography is not his strength: he sends the tablets and cipher to Stanwad, though that colleague’s expedition has also fallen silent, and arranges transport through McGoyver.
Rowan Helfgot is affiliated with the Royal Stormwind Society of Science and is stationed at Valgarde.
A Valgarde yeoman stationed at the settlement.
A cannoneer stationed at Valgarde.
A Valgarde yeoman stationed at the settlement.
A Dragonflayer raider operating in Howling Fjord.
A plagued Dragonflayer tribesman on the Chillmere Coast, whose loss of self-control turns him against friend and foe alike.
A Longtusk fisherman found on the Chillmere Coast, this humanoid is one of the named fishing folk in the area.
An unstable Mur'ghoul found on the Chillmere Coast, this undead creature is one of several Mur'ghoul types in the same coastal area.
A Mur'ghoul flesheater found on the Chillmere Coast, this undead creature is one of the named Mur'ghoul types present in the area.
A Mur'ghoul corrupter encountered on the Chillmere Coast, it is among the Scourge types Explorer Jaren asks adventurers to fight while they transform murlocs and other creatures into undead.
A Dragonflayer tribesman fighting on the Chillmere Coast, this combatant cries allegiance to Ymiron, taunts opponents, and charges nearby enemies.
A Dragonflayer Vrykul encountered in Howling Fjord. In combat it can use Chop and Throw; being hit by Plague Spray triggers it to cast Spray Credit.
A Winterskorn spearman, a humanoid fighter found in several areas of Howling Fjord.
A Dragonflayer Warrior in Nifflevar, one of the settlement's defenders Ranger Captain Areiel seeks to weaken before an Alliance advance.
A Winterskorn Bonegrinder encountered in Howling Fjord.

In Nifflevar, a Dragonflayer Rune-Seer taunts a Valgarde captive, calling outsiders weak before remarking that they are hardier than their size suggests. Ranger Captain Areiel includes Rune-Seers among the town's defenders she wants weakened before an Alliance advance.
A Winterskorn Skald encountered in Howling Fjord.

A Dragonflayer Death Weaver serving Ymiron, this combatant uses shadow magic in battle, casting Shadow Bolt and preparing Soul Infusion outside combat. Its cries pledge its life to Ymiron and threaten opponents, marking it as a loyal fighter.
A Dragonflayer Thane serving Ymiron, this combatant uses Sunder Armor and Hamstring in battle. Its shared cries pledge its life to Ymiron and threaten opponents, presenting a loyal warrior role.
A Winterskorn combatant who rallies behind Ymiron and threatens foes. Its battle cries frame it as a fighter in the ruler's service.

A Winterskorn fighter serving Ymiron, the Woodsman throws weapons in combat and joins its fellows in threatening foes and rallying to their ruler. Its battle role presents a faction combatant rather than an individually characterized figure.

A Winterskorn Shield-Maiden who fights with a thrown shield, she pledges her life to Ymiron, rallies for him, and taunts opponents in battle. Her cries and combat role present a committed fighter in Ymiron's service.
A Winterskorn Warrior fights for Ymiron, declaring “My life for Ymiron!” and “For Ymiron!” It threatens its foes with “Die, maggot!”
A Winterskorn Raider fights for Ymiron, declaring “My life for Ymiron!” and “For Ymiron!” It threatens foes and can use Kick against a casting target.
A Winterskorn Berserker fights for Ymiron, declaring “My life for Ymiron!” and “For Ymiron!” It threatens its foes with “Die, maggot!”
A Winterskorn Rune-Seer fights for Ymiron, declaring “My life for Ymiron!” and “For Ymiron!” It can cast Rune Ward in combat.
A Winterskorn Rune-Caster fights for Ymiron and threatens foes with “I will break you!” It can cast Frost Shock and Frostbolt in combat.
A Winterskorn oracle in Howling Fjord.

The Winterskorn Elder is a fierce fighter devoted to Ymiron, shouting that its life is his and threatening to break or eat its foes. It also voices contempt for the small creatures it faces. In combat it can cast Earth Shield and Lightning Bolt, giving it both protective and offensive capabilities.
An Iron Rune Worker, this dwarf's remarks include an apology for insolence and a promise that the Iron Rune will double its efforts. Those lines suggest a subordinate in an organized workforce.

An Iron Rune Steelguard, this dwarf challenges unfamiliar arrivals, demands identification and warns that its section is off-limits. It also apologizes for insolence and promises that the Iron Rune will double its efforts, suggesting a guard who serves within an organized force.

Iron Rune Sage is the name used for one of the iron dwarves targeted at Ivald's Ruin. Donny describes the iron dwarves there as trying to bury the site and its relics, and includes the Sages among the targets he wants removed.

An Iron Rune Runemaster, this dwarf challenges unfamiliar arrivals, demands identification and warns that its section is off-limits. It also apologizes for insolence and promises that the Iron Rune will double its efforts, suggesting a guard who serves within an organized force.
An iron dwarf at Ivald's Ruin, among the steel-skinned figures Donny says are burying the site rather than excavating it. Donny calls for the destroyers to be killed as part of stopping that work.
Frost Nymph, a humanoid in Howling Fjord.
Recently freed from danger, this Chill Nymph credits Lurielle for sending help, thanks her rescuer, and longs to see her sisters again.
A Plagued Proto-Dragon found in Borean Tundra. When it bears the Radiation aura, it casts Radiation.
A proto-whelp of the Ember Clutch. Captain Adams describes the clutch's growing blaze as a threat and asks that its eggs and whelps be destroyed to contain it.

An Ember Clutch proto-drake that Malister fears may continue attacking Westguard Keep after humans roused the clutch. He reluctantly asks for its destruction and gives the adventurer a wand to draw its attention; when led in pursuit, it casts Overpowering Sickness.
Shoveltusks are tusked animals hunted for their meat around Howling Fjord. They can headbutt attackers.
Shoveltusk Stags are animals found around Howling Fjord. They defend themselves with a forceful gore.
Duskwing Eagles are wild birds found in parts of Howling Fjord.
Iron Rune Laborers are iron dwarves working at Ivald's Ruin. Donny says they are burying the site rather than excavating it.
The Stone Giant is a powerful stone creature found in Howling Fjord.

Guard Captain Zorek is an Alliance officer at Valgarde who steels his troops against fear of the Lich King and the deaths their service may bring. His plan for payback against the vrykul harpoon crews depends on recovering their weapon manual and control mechanism; he arranges for a gryphon to carry the mechanism to Lieutenant Icehammer. He relishes the troops’ success against the Dragonflayer leader Ingvar.

Baron Ulrik von Stromhearth represents the Kirin Tor and offers teleportation to Dalaran. The baron explains that the city moved from beneath its protective dome at Lordamere Lake to float above Crystalsong Forest, and sends travelers to Archmage Celindra with a personal signet as proof of their meeting.

Harold Lagras is a hesitant, evasive worker whom Keller has sent to recover Valgarde supplies from Daggercap Bay shipwrecks. He calls the crates “goodies,” then boasts that documenting them is beyond the player's training and dismisses them with “Skedaddle!”

Innkeeper Hazel Lagras runs an inn she says was built before the northern savages awoke. She welcomes visitors and asks whether they will stay long; her remark also shows that she views the awakening in the north with apprehension.
Sorely Twitchblade supplies poison components. His warning that dealing with poison and alcohol is dangerous comes out in a drunken, hiccupping slur, giving his brief exchange a wry edge.
Horatio is a stable boy who calls himself a stable master, but still imagines what he will be when he grows up: “a stable man.”

Anchorite Yazmina is a first aid trainer who tends wounded soldiers: she changes bandages, treats infection, and worries that scarce medical supplies will keep her from caring for everyone properly. She reassures one soldier that she will take care of them, though Northrend's cold taxes her too.
Bartleby Armorfist is an armorsmith in Valgarde who offers armor goods and repairs.
Pricilla Winterwind is Valgarde’s gryphon master and offers fast travel. When attacked, she calls for guards and summons an enraged gryphon.

Coot “The Stranger” Albertson is Valgarde’s bartender, known for serving booze and offering wary advice: he warns against trusting gnomes. His greetings sometimes suggest he does not recognize a visitor.
Foreman Miles McMoody is a named foreman in Valgarde.
Valgarde Defenders are soldiers holding the gate against monsters. Their battle calls urge troops to stand firm and fire, and one identifies a beast’s eyes as a vulnerable spot.
Frosthorn rams are animal beasts found across several Northrend areas.
Icehollow Behemoths are hulking creatures found in the Icehollow area.

Captain Adams is an Alliance officer at Westguard Keep, coordinating its response to the vrykul and other threats. He repeatedly entrusts the adventurer with dangerous operations, values their help, and asks for news from the field. His brisk, sometimes sharp replies show a commander under pressure who takes reports seriously.
Blockade Pirate is one of the pirate combatants holding the blockade in the Shattered Straits, where Alliance forces use cluster bombs against the fleet.
Forsaken Plaguebringers fight with Shoot Plague and Wandering Plague.

Cannoneer Ely serves at Westguard Keep, where the keep’s cannons need ammunition. He complains that their non-standard size requires specially made cannonballs and sends people to recover rounds already fired toward the south and east. He is running low while the fighting around Skorn continues, and ruefully calls recovery duty unlike what he signed up for.

Chef Kettleblack is responsible for feeding the people at Westguard Keep. With livestock disappearing, she needs shoveltusk meat for the keep’s meals and warns that the stags are dangerous. She takes pride in the meat’s quality, but her own words show frustration at carrying the cooking, cleaning, and everything else; after receiving the meat, she quietly offers the visitor some.
This Dark Ranger is an elite humanoid combatant.

A Proto-Drake Egg of the Ember Clutch in the burning forest southeast of Westguard Keep. Captain Adams describes the clutch as ablaze and its eggs as part of a spreading threat; adventurers are tasked with destroying them.

Dark Ranger Lyana is a Forsaken commander at the Bleeding Vale, directing attacks on Alliance forces at the Derelict Strand. She orders a strike against their leaders and the marking of their cannons, and praises the Banshee Queen. Her battlefield calls press her troops to hold the enemy apart and stop reinforcements. She regards the stranded sailors as tenacious, though doomed, and expects the surrounded Alliance force to be crushed.
A Vengeance Landing Deathguard, one of several stationed in the settlement in Howling Fjord. This is a humanoid combatant.

High Executor Anselm is a veteran Forsaken commander at Vengeance Landing. He says he has fought under many banners, but this campaign against Arthas is finally his own: he wants the Lich King dead and treats the Alliance as an obstacle. He directs his officers against the Alliance and orders a public strike on Prince Keleseth and the vrykul at Utgarde. The bodies left by the fighting concern him because the dead can rise as weapons, so he orders them burned. He values discipline and the chain of command, rebuking newcomers who assume their past deeds put them above orders; revenge against Arthas remains personal.
Apothecary Celestine is an apothecary associated with the Royal Apothecary Society.
This injured defender is one of six wounded fighters represented in the area, a casualty within the local defensive force.

Apothecary Hanes is a Royal Apothecary Society apothecary held by Alliance forces at the Derelict Strand. During his escape, he urges setting fire to the camp’s limited supplies and openly welcomes revenge against his captors. He directs his rescuer to speak with Lysander at Vengeance Landing about a reward.
A Daggercap hammerhead is a local hammerhead shark.
A Valgarde laborer is part of the settlement’s working population.
A North Fleet soldier serves with the fleet’s fighting force.
A North Fleet medic serves the fleet in a medical role, tending its personnel.
An Iron Rune Binder is a binder among the Iron Rune.
Wink Sprinklesprankle is a general goods and trade supplies vendor in Howling Fjord. Visitors can browse his goods.

Orfus of Kamagua is a tuskarr who came with his son to investigate reports of the dead rising near Shield Hill. He seeks to recover stolen burial artifacts and return them to their resting places to calm the spirits, and warns travelers away from the danger. He also urges his people to seek Elder Atuik's help against the Northsea Freebooters.
A mechanical cannon controller associated with Vengeance Landing's cannons.
A Vengeance Landing cannoneer found in the Howling Fjord.
Camille is the Forsaken bat handler at Vengeance Landing. Her greeting asks whether travelers seek passage and says her bats will get them there in no time.
The Valgarde Harpoon Target is a mechanical target that casts Torch when hit by Blazing Harpoon.

Harrowmeiser is a captured zeppelin owner, held at the dock after his craft was shot down while ferrying Horde personnel and supplies. He resents being made to circle the bay for the anti-pirate bombing run, complains that the damaged zeppelin lacks parts, and protests that he is a prisoner. His remarks give its departure timing and invite someone to set him free.

Old Man Stonemantle is an elderly father worried about his daughter, Overseer Irena Stonemantle, who leads an Explorers' League party at Steel Gate. He asks for news of her after hearing that explorers at Whisper Gulch have gone mad. Despite his age, he remains captivated by the frontier, though he fears its evil and dangerous knowledge.

Explorer Jaren is Irena Stonemantle's betrothed, investigating artifact rumors on the Chillmere Coast. He finds Scourge transforming the coast's murlocs and urges action against them and their crystals. While hiding from danger, he keeps his voice low; he is relieved to hear Irena sent help and asks that she be told he is safe.
A Westguard lumberjack, stationed among the lumberjacks in the Westguard area.
A Westguard cannoneer, stationed among the cannoneers in the Westguard area.
A Westguard crossbowman stationed in Howling Fjord.
A Westguard defender whose brief reactions show surprise at an unexpected ability and interest in what is happening.
A Westguard officer serving with the defenders, who checks with concern whether someone is okay.
A Westguard cavalryman, a mounted soldier serving with Westguard's force.

Greer Orehammer is Westguard Keep's gryphon master and an established contact for Alliance travel and urgent deliveries. When the Alliance missive reaches him, he reads it and stresses that its warning must reach High Commander Wyrmbane quickly, offering his fastest gryphon for the trip to Wintergarde. He handles flight travel, and responds to a request for a gryphon and bombs against New Agamand by supplying bombs. If attacked, he calls for the guards.
Lissan White, a humanoid found in Howling Fjord.

Finlay Fletcher maintains Westguard Keep's crossbows and makes ammunition; his assistant has been commandeered for the move to Fort Wildervaar, leaving him short of catgut. He ruefully notes that he spends his days making ammo and restringing crossbows, then asks whether you want him to do something as well.
Vengeance Bringer, a humanoid found in Howling Fjord.
A North Fleet sailor found around Vengeance Landing and its neighboring area, this sailor attacks when out of combat.

An ancient of the Ember Clutch, this proto-drake brood's woods-wise guardian sees nature as a balance and blames the newly awakened vrykul and their master for disturbing it. It argues that killing the handlers is the proper way to curb the threat, while doubting the woods' creatures will live peacefully with the vrykul reawakened. It addresses the player as “little one.”

A Dragonflayer handler operating in the Ember Clutch, among the newly awakened vrykul whose presence is disturbing the woods. The Root Causes quest names handlers as targets in the effort to stop the vrykul expansion.
A thorn-covered creature of the Twisted Glade, among the beasts blamed for murdering the glade’s sisters. It casts Thorns when out of combat.
A spore creature found in the Twisted Glade. It releases a cloud of spores when fighting.
A tamed proto-whelp found in the Dragonblight.
A Forsaken crossbowman. When struck by Vampire Soul Retrieve Channel, it casts Suicide.
The Bull Lion Seal is a beast found in the Howling Fjord.
The Lion Seal is a beast found in the Howling Fjord.

Mage-Lieutenant Malister serves at Westguard Keep, where he advises the captain and sometimes disagrees with his decisions. He regrets the attack on the proto-drakes and calls the resulting need to kill them shameful. He also presses for action against the dormant vrykul beneath Gjalerbron and studies plans concerning the frost wyrm Glacion. His comments show a cautious, reflective officer who weighs the consequences of military choices.

Overseer Irena Stonemantle leads an Explorers' League operation at Steel Gate. She says the work is just beginning, but worsening trouble in Rivenwood may force them home before it is finished; too few qualified pilots also slow the operation. Her fiancé, Explorer Jaren, went with a small group to investigate artifact rumors on Chillmere Coast, and she fears for the explorers amid the murlocs there. She resents her father's overprotectiveness, though she is glad of help.

Bombardier Petrov directs bombing efforts against the pirate blockade in the Shattered Straits. He urges the player to use cluster bombs from a zeppelin Harrowmeiser has loaned, calling the mission vital to breaking the blockade. Petrov expects further runs once more bombs are ready; his assistant, Feknut, is collecting bat guano for the next batch. His speech is brisk and enthusiastic about striking the pirates.

Scout Knowles watches Halgrind from the cover of an abandoned Vrykul tower, where he investigates Forsaken activity for Captain Adams. He has spotted plague tanks and an apothecary taken into Halgrind, and speaks with practical urgency about disrupting the Forsaken’s plans. His knowledge comes from what he can observe nearby; the tower's cover keeps him at a distance.
Jhet Ironbeard supplies blacksmithing goods and offers repairs in Howling Fjord.
Westguard workers are present around the keep in numbers, carrying out the labor that supports the settlement.
An Ice Elemental is an elemental creature found across Northrend.
Giant Tidecrawlers are a creature population.
A trained plaguehound is a beast.
Yanis the Mystic bears the title Herald of Ingvar. He is a humanoid whose combat actions include throwing a Dragonflayer harpoon and using Intercept.
A humanoid salvager identified by the occupational label North Fleet Salvager.
A Val'kyr Watcher, identified by a role of keeping watch.
Innkeeper Celeste Goodhutch offers lodging and food at her inn. She warmly tells visitors they deserve rest, food and relaxation.

Pontius keeps plaguehounds at Vengeance Landing for military scouting, but insists they must be fed properly before they will cooperate. He asks visitors to hunt crows for them and recalls raising purebreds in Tirisfal. He says normal dogs now avoid him, so plaguehounds have become a substitute; he jokes self-deprecatingly about their looks and his own.
A demon known simply as a Fiend.

Skeld Drakeson is a newly awakened vrykul master whose presence is driving the expansion of the magically burning woods around Ember Clutch. The Ember Clutch Ancient identifies him as one of the real causes of the disturbance and directs the player to his lair on the clutch’s south side.
A fjord crow in the Howling Fjord, this bird reacts to the “Sic’em” spell by attacking the spell’s invoker.
A North Fleet marksman in the Howling Fjord. This humanoid is stationed in the Westguard area and serves as a ranged combatant for the fleet.
Riven Widow is a bat associated with the Darkclaw bats of Rivenwood. Darkclaw Guano is obtained from it for Engineer Feknut’s request for bat guano.
Darkclaw Bats are beasts found across several areas of this zone.
Captain Olster is named as an enemy leader at the Derelict Strand. Dark Ranger Lyana's mission calls for his assassination alongside Lieutenant Celeyne and Sergeant Lorric, listing him first by rank.
Sergeant Lorric is named among the enemy leaders at the Derelict Strand. Dark Ranger Lyana's assassination mission ranks him after Captain Olster and Lieutenant Celeyne.
Lieutenant Celeyne is named among the enemy leaders at the Derelict Strand. Dark Ranger Lyana's assassination mission ranks her between Captain Olster and Sergeant Lorric.

The Deranged Explorer bears the Explorers' League affiliation, but speaks in fractured pleas to forget, laughter about finding secrets, and threats toward those who know “the truth.” At close range it uses Sunder Armor and a torch.

Thoralius the Wise at Valgarde believes the spirits hold knowledge of Northrend’s past, present and future. With incense and proper reagents, he seeks visions of that world. Too old and weak to survive another journey himself, he sends others to investigate Wyrmskull and Nifflevar, puzzled that visions show vrykul from 15,000 years ago despite their apparently recent arrival.

Sapper Steelring is a former Explorers' League sapper who escaped Whisper Gulch when his fellow explorers went mad. The captain sends him to recover ore and gems from the gulch and target his old boss, Squeeg Idolhunter. Steelring is practical and openly interested in profit, but the strange ore unsettles him; he is also glad to have survived.

Abandoned Pack Mules are pack animals taken into Whisper Gulch with Explorers' League equipment. Abigail says they can be spooked back by a raised hand; they are her concern as she tries to recover the keep's lost supplies.

Explorer Abigail is trying to recover the mules and equipment taken into Whisper Gulch with most of the Explorers' League. Their loss threatens efforts to rebuild, while the gulch's unknown discovery troubles her enough to keep her awake imagining it. She asks for help recovering the mules.
A Forsaken deckhand serving among the Forsaken forces in Northrend.

A North Fleet marine serving aboard the fleet's ships. Captain Harker identifies the marines as Alliance forces who boarded his ships during an ambush, leaving his side needing help to retake them and restore its cannon fire.
A pack mule kept at Westguard, associated by name with the Explorers' League.
A Westguard stable eagle.
A Westguard stable ram.
A Westguard stable horse.

A Gjalerbron vrykul sleep-watcher among the fortress’s hostile inhabitants. Captain Adams and Chieftain Ashtotem each identify sleep-watchers as targets in their calls to stop Gjalerbron’s vrykul and their unexplained activity. This watcher’s combat cries threaten to eat or gut intruders.

A Gjalerbron vrykul rune-caster and one of the fortress’s hostile inhabitants. Captain Adams and Chieftain Ashtotem name rune-casters among their targets as they seek to stop the vrykul’s unexplained activity. This caster greets intruders with contempt and threats, including a boast about making a necklace from their entrails.
A Gjalerbron warrior serving Ymiron, this vrykul fights with threats of feeding intruders to the dogs or eating their hearts. Its battle cry pledges its life to Ymiron.

Putrid Wights are Scourge undead found at Gjalerbron, including in the Waking Halls below it. Father Levariol and Greatmother Ankha both call for their destruction, framing the threat against the Light and the natural spirits respectively.
An elite sepulchral overseer encountered in the Gjalerbron region. Its title marks an overseeing role.
A Dragonflayer hunting hound found at Nifflevar. Ranger Captain Areiel identifies it among the forces to be reduced before the Alliance can gain an advantage over the town.

Deathstalker Razael is a Forsaken field officer at the Bleeding Vale. He reports that frozen ground has left the meatwagons immobile and his forces exposed, while Alliance survivors hold defenses at the Derelict Strand. High Executor Anselm seeks his report on the fighting.
An Alliance corpse is a body that can be targeted for a burn-body interaction.
A Forsaken corpse is a body that can be targeted for a burn-body interaction.
A Deathless Watcher is a Scourge creature found at Gjalerbron. It lies submerged while undisturbed and rises when engaged.
Necrolords serve the Lich King and threaten to make their foes serve him too. Their battle cries promise that another life will join his ranks.
Winterskorn Defenders threaten intruders with impalement and feed their fallen to sharks at Daggercap. Their taunts frame outsiders as sacrifices who have come to them.

Ulf the Bloodletter is named in Gorth’s campaign against the Winterskorn Vrykul, alongside Oric the Baleful and Gunnar Thorvardsson. Gorth calls these foes the “hero vrykuls” and urges planting the Forsaken banner on their corpses.

Necro Overlord Mezhen leads the necrolords at Gjalerbron. Mezhen boasts that opponents cannot stop what is already set in motion and threatens them with doom. Captain Adams suspects the necrolords are working to bring the vrykul into Arthas’s fold, while Chieftain Ashtotem fears their cooperation with undead forces.

Glacion is an undead frost wyrm whose master is Wyrmcaller Vile. Celea Frozenmane and Mage-Lieutenant Malister believe, from captured plans, that Vile’s horn can call Glacion back to Gjalerbron. They seek the wyrm’s destruction and the horn’s recovery to keep it from returning to the wrong hands.

Queen Angerboda is performing a ritual at Winter's Terrace to awaken her husband-king, Ymiron. She calls him her love and promises that, with the Lich King's might behind him, the world will tremble. She demands souls and more sacrifices to speed the rite, and warns that her work will not be stopped.
A Fanggore Worg is a Northrend beast that can provide chilled meat, an ingredient travelers can bring to Brom Brewbaster for cooking.

Sergeant Gorth directs attacks against the Winterskorn across the blockade and in Baleheim. He wants to frighten them by killing their strongest vrykul and putting the queen's flag on their corpses; he also proposes burning the town's buildings and bridges. His speech is blunt and ungrammatical. He says the Forsaken put him back together, admits he misses fighting now that he is a sergeant, and boasts that his side looks better than the vrykul. He praises successful work even when the burning is incomplete.
At Camp Winterhoof, Talu Frosthoof is a bowyer who sells goods and ammunition and offers repairs.
At Gjalerbron, Wyrmcaller Vile is identified as the master of the frost wyrm Glacion. He taunts an opponent about their hope of saving friends and wields frost magic.
Iron Rune Stonecallers cast Summon Stone Giant out of combat.
Camp Winterhoof Braves are humanoid combatants stationed near the camp.

Celea Frozenmane is Camp Winterhoof’s wind rider master. When shown the Gjalerbron attack plans, she reacts with alarm and urges that the threat be stopped. On hearing that the danger has passed, she says the camp will soon move on and expresses surprise that visitors from across the ocean may not be so bad after all.
Bori Wintertotem is an innkeeper whose welcome centers on shelter and rest from the cold. He offers hospitality to weary visitors at his establishment.
The Gjalerbron Prisoners are captives held by the vrykul at Gjalerbron, where living sacrifices fuel an awakening ritual. Their words mourn friends already sacrificed and thank a rescuer.

Captain Harker commands the Forsaken fleet near the Derelict Strand. After Alliance boarders seize its ships, he urges their recovery so the cannons can fire again; he mocks the boarders and presses the fight against the Alliance and Arthas.

Father Levariol is a priest who invokes the Light in blessing and treats the Scourge and Gjalerbron's vrykul rites as threats. He urges the freeing of captives and the destruction of Scourge, then studies an ascension scroll and suspects the thane's ritual could transcend death. He frames these dangers as matters of faith and holy duty.

McGoyver supplies dark iron ingots for Walt's rebuilding project and can fly travelers between the dig-site area and the Explorers' League Outpost. He has a quirky, comic edge: he may offer a garbled refusal to fly or greet someone with “Evenin', Gov'na.”
Squeeg Idolhunter is an Explorers' League figure who uses dynamite in battle.
Wildervar Sentries are guards stationed around Wildervar, forming part of the area's defensive presence. Their identity is defined by the sentry role and post.
Dragonflayer Invaders fight in Ymiron's name, shouting their loyalty to him and contempt for their foes. They are part of the force attacking Valgarde and use charging attacks in battle.

Eldrim Mounder is the fort's blacksmith, blunt and impatient with requests beyond his work. He tells would-be settlers to build within the fort, refuses mule shoeing, and says the forge is reserved for expedition business. He also sells goods and repairs equipment.
Helga Rumsbane is the fort's General Goods vendor, providing everyday supplies to the expedition community. Her role centers on keeping general provisions available to people in the settlement.
Balar Rumsbane is the fort's Trade Goods vendor, supplying trade goods to the expedition community. His shop provides a source of merchandise for people in the settlement.
Drogan Ironshaper, a humanoid found in Howling Fjord.

Christopher Sloan is a fisherman at Fort Wildervar, tired of filling barrels of salted fish and longing to return to fishing for his dinner. He praises Nat Pagle’s bait, but fears Frostfin after the monster nearly dragged him into the lake. With the expedition expected to pass through, he recruits help to secure bait and make fishing possible again.

Christina Daniels is an innkeeper who welcomes weary travelers to her inn. She helps guests settle in, offers goods, and is associated with the Trick or Treat tradition. Her greeting is warm and direct, opening with an offer to help.
A Wildervar worker among the many workers found in the area.

The Westguard Sergeant is a defensive officer who offers to assist and defend visitors and invites their orders. In a Skorn operation, his instructions call for cannon support against the towers; after a separate machete task, he watches warily and asks for his blade back.
James Ormsby is a named gryphon master who offers fast travel. When threatened, he calls for guards and summons an enraged gryphon.
Wildervar Miner is a miner found in the Wildervar region.
Artie Grizzlehand is a stable master associated with pet stabling and help recovering lost companions.
Mahana Frosthoof is a stable master associated with pet stabling and help recovering lost companions.
Fearsome Horrors are hostile creatures listed among the Scourge targets at Gjalerbron in Father Levariol's request to clear the lair.
A wild worg of the Winterskorn, found in the surrounding lands.

An impaled Valgarde scout left gravely wounded, with no hope of surviving. Before death, he fears for the citizens held in cages and longs for his family to know what happened. He asks a stranger to avenge him.
An assistant of the Royal Apothecary Society, stationed in the Howling Fjord. The supplied records establish her Society affiliation but give no personal history or specific duties.
A Valgarde priest held captive in the Howling Fjord. The records identify the prisoner's religious role, but provide no individual history or further details.
A Valgarde mage held captive in the Howling Fjord. The records identify the prisoner's magical role, but provide no individual history or further details.
A Valgarde warrior held captive in the Howling Fjord. The records identify the prisoner's martial role, but provide no individual history or further details.
A Valgarde paladin held captive in the Howling Fjord. The records identify the prisoner's sacred role, but provide no individual history or further details.
A New Agamand deathguard in Howling Fjord.

Scout Valory is a scout working among the remaining veteran guards at Wyrmskull Village. After the scouts' inspection found most of their people slain or captured, Valory sends the player to investigate sounds of fighting to the northeast and look for survivors or useful intelligence. Their words convey urgency, with the crisis still uncontrolled.

Defender Mordun is a veteran defender who has fought the vrykul and fears their numbers and appetite for battle will overwhelm his side. He regards Ingvar's standing among them as a chance to damage their morale, and warns that their unusually deadly, well-balanced weapons may be unnatural. Mordun speaks bluntly in a rough sailor's dialect, and mourns the loss of his best men.
A Dragonflayer oracle lies dead in Howling Fjord.
A Dragonflayer thane lies dead in Howling Fjord.
A Valgarde defender lies dead in Howling Fjord.
A Winterskorn scout, identified by name as part of the Winterskorn group. This individual is in Howling Fjord.

Lurielle is a member of a sisterhood in the Frozen Glade, whose queen has forbidden contact with outsiders. As upheaval endangers her sisters and changes the glades, she reaches out for help. She remembers the ice elementals as former companions and keeps their cores in hope of restoring them; she also refuses to give up hope for her afflicted sisters and the glade's redemption.

Pulroy is an Explorers' League dwarf archaeologist whose expedition to Wyrmskull Village was attacked. He and Zedd had discovered a cipher for the tablets before they were separated; Pulroy was later found dead, still gripping his journal.

Nokoma Snowseer is a Camp Winterhoof hunter preparing for her first giant-yeti hunt. She doubts the elders' claim that her dire-ram horn mimics a female yeti's mating call. After hearing the test report that the beast spoke, she questions continuing and plans to consult Chief Ashtotem. As a child she searched for frost nymphs and nearly froze; their recent appearance now concerns her.

Cormath the Courier is a traveler through Howling Fjord whose journeys revealed Camp Winterhoof, a settlement he describes as tauren-like from afar but sturdier and shaggier up close. He sends the traveler to Chieftain Ashtotem to make contact and assess whether the settlement can be of use.

Apothecary Lysander is a Royal Apothecary Society plague researcher working from Vengeance Landing. He worries that the sea voyage has weakened their plague and seeks toxins and human test subjects to strengthen and assess it. His brisk, morbid enthusiasm treats infection and casualties as measures of progress.

Ahota Whitefrost is a Camp Winterhoof warrior who helps prepare his people for a seasonal trek into the hills, gathering hippogryph down for clothing and equipment. He openly favors standing their ground over abandoning the post and argues that dormant vrykul beneath Gjalerbron must be stopped before the necrolords awaken them.

Chieftain Ashtotem leads the taunka of Camp Winterhoof as the vrykul and the dead threaten the Howling Fjord. He says trust among his people is earned and allows an outsider to help as they prepare to leave for safer lands to the north. Reports from his longrunners about strange rituals at Gjalerbron trouble him, and he wants the threat stopped before it reaches his people.

The Winterhoof Brave is a taunka fighter who helps defend his people and strike at the vrykul threat around Skorn. He worries the vrykul may rise again after death, and gives practical aid for the fight, including a machete for dismembering their remains. His words show grim resolve about making the vrykul feel the danger they would bring to others.

Trapper Jethan is based at Fort Wildervar and came from the Grizzly Hills to trade with his people’s outpost. He sets traps in nearby woods and snowy areas, bartering the captured creatures’ meat and fur with townspeople. He offers a share of his profits for help gathering prey, while warning that other predators may reach the traps first.

Greatmother Ankha is an elder at Camp Winterhoof, worried about her son Sage Mistwalker after he left with longrunners to investigate a recurring wolf vision near Steel Gate. She urges the release of captives at Gjalerbron regardless of who they are and opposes the vrykul rites and Scourge there. She studies signs that the vrykul may seek to transcend death; her people are preparing to journey north.

Gil Grisert is a Fort Wildervar cloak-maker under pressure to prepare gear before Captain Adams's force moves north. He worries about the captain's temper while trying to finish the order. After learning Steelfeather is a mother, Gil suggests leaving her nest undisturbed and ribs Jethan for wanting a trophy.
Stephen Barone is a general goods vendor.
A Camp Winterhoof Wind Rider is a humanoid associated with Camp Winterhoof.

Zedd is an Explorers’ League member who worked with Pulroy to decipher tablets in Wyrmskull. Pulroy reports that they were separated while Zedd carried the cipher. Zedd is found apparently dead near the worgs; a nearby message points toward Glorenfeld and Daegarn in the catacombs.
Tara Cooper is a trade goods vendor.
David Marks is a poison vendor. Visitors can browse his goods.

Basil Osgood is an innkeeper with a practical, hospitable welcome: he invites weary travelers to rest and lets guests make his inn their home. His counter also offers goods, and he takes part in seasonal Trick or Treat festivities.

Glorenfeld is an Explorers’ League dwarf working among the relics at Utgarde Catacombs. The loss of two fellow dwarves weighs on him, but he stays focused on recovering the tablets and rescuing Daegarn, whose cipher is needed to understand the find. His matter-of-fact humor surfaces even amid the danger.

Daegarn is an Explorers’ League dwarf caught in Dragonflayer captivity at Utgarde Catacombs. He is blunt and defiant, demanding release and challenging his captors; he also asks what happened to the people of the village. Despite the danger, he remains absorbed in a discovery he calls the missing link to humankind. His beard was searched for the cipher, which is now with Oluf.

At the Apothecary Camp, Royal Apothecary Society member Apothecary Malthus investigates what is driving the Explorers' League mad, suspecting the beer in Whisper Gulch's kegs. After tasting it, he insists it is ordinary beer and warns you not to tell Grick. He also dismisses the northern bison-men as reclusive and says the land will soon change.

Tobias Sarkhoff is a bat handler at New Agamand who offers air travel. His replies about the Blight specimen are breezy and trusting: he says you can keep the vial, then jokes about arranging delivery of highly lethal poisonous gas to Venomspite.

Plaguebringer Tillinghast of the Royal Apothecary Society dreams of extending the plague beyond humanoids to any creature. He devises tests on proto-whelps and proto-drakes, treating danger to his assistant as the price of progress. Disappointing results leave him distraught, fearing that news of his failure will ruin his standing among the apothecaries.
A Dragonflayer Oracle in the Dragonflayer region of Howling Fjord.

Oric the Baleful threatens to tear enemies of the Winterskorn limb from limb. Gorth identifies Oric among the powerful vrykul heroes whose deaths are meant to teach the others to fear the Forsaken. Oric fights with Cleave and Mortal Strike.

Gunnar Thorvardsson announces himself as Gunnar, son of Thorvard, and threatens opponents with death. Gorth names him among the powerful vrykul heroes whose deaths are meant to make the others fear the Forsaken.
Apothecary Dorne serves the Royal Apothecary Society.

Micah Stonebreaker is a dwarf held in a cage, coughing and shivering as he weakly shakes its bars. His outbursts protest the spraying and invoke Brann’s beard, conveying a distressed, desperate response to whoever is tormenting him.
A Dragonflayer Lieutenant is a humanoid combatant encountered in the region. In battle it casts Head Slash, giving this rank a clear fighting role.
The Daggercap Hawk is a wild bird found across the surrounding region. It appears in several local areas and is a low-level creature, part of the area's ordinary wildlife.
The Fjord Rat is a tiny local animal found across many nearby areas. A critter, it is a familiar part of the region’s wildlife.

Foreman Colbey runs the mine near Fort Wildervar, where his crew is mining ore for the expeditionary force’s weapons. A yeti has blocked the tunnel they need, and Colbey asks for help to rouse it. He is anxious about the delay and the prospect of explaining to Captain Adams why the weapons are not ready.
The Decomposing Ghoul is a widespread creature that speaks both out of combat and in response to Shining Light. Its reaction includes cries about the bright light and warnings to go away.

Shatterhorn is a giant yeti that sleeps in the mine across the bridge from Fort Wildervar, blocking its expansion tunnel. Fresh ram meat wakes him; when engaged, he roars and can use Ground Smash. His behavior is that of a dangerous creature disturbed from sleep, rather than a speaking quest giver.

Sage Mistwalker is troubled by dreams of Ulfang, his worg life-friend, calling for help. He seeks to reach him through Rivenwood, using meditation to prepare an outsider and a fragile magical worg disguise. Dwarven excavation of artifacts near Steel Gate also angers him; he wants their significance understood.
Samuel Rosemond is a Provisioner who sells goods and ammunition and repairs equipment.

Ares the Oathbound is an Argent Crusade envoy carrying a sacred duty in the Utgarde Catacombs: recover a cleansed artifact from the den of the dead and return it to Lord Irulon Trueblade. His account recalls the Plaguelands' heavy losses, and he invokes the Light as protection. He urges the bearer to fight with honor.

Lord Irulon Trueblade is an Argent Crusade lord in Northrend. “Guided by Honor” names him as the recipient of a recovered sacred blade, intended for Tirion Fordring as the Crusade works toward Icecrown.
A Winterhoof Longrunner in Howling Fjord.
A trapped animal found across several areas of Northrend.
A Westguard rifleman, representing the armed force named by Westguard.

A Plagued Dragonflayer Rune-Caster is one of the afflicted Dragonflayers in the Rivenwood. When its self-control breaks, it attacks friend and foe alike, making the plague a danger even to those around it.

A Plagued Dragonflayer Handler is an afflicted Dragonflayer found in the Rivenwood. Like the rune-casters nearby, it can lose all self-control and attack friend and foe alike; its handler name distinguishes its role.

Longrunner Skycloud is a Winterhoof hunting leader at Steel Gate, left guarding the small force still with him after the Rivenwood widows devastated his hunters. He fears the Scourge has stirred the creatures nearby and hopes his missing longrunners survived inside the cocoons. Their slow venom makes him wary of the spiders, and he warns others to avoid the Rivenwood.
An Iron Rune Guardian is a sentinel associated with the iron runes of Howling Fjord.

A Dragonflayer Berserker is a hostile warrior who fights for King Ymiron. Its battle cries urge its kin to savor their enemies' misery and threaten captives, reflecting the brutal manner of the Dragonflayer forces in Howling Fjord.

At the Apothecary Camp, Grick doubts Malthus’s theory that stealing the dwarves’ beer will solve the mystery. He wants brains for experiments that might reveal what is happening and provide a new plague component, so he sends an adventurer to harvest them from the dwarves.
A Dragonflayer held captive in the region.

Engineer Feknut is at Steel Gate, where Petrov sent him to collect bat guano for cluster bombs. Feknut is afraid to leave his platform, so he asks an adventurer to scare guano from the bats with firecrackers. He complains about Petrov and the other explorers, and his dialogue has him urging them to leave.

An ice elemental found in the snowy hills around the outpost and elsewhere in the region. Wind Tamer Kagan includes iceshard elementals among the creatures whose growing numbers pose an environmental danger to the camp; this elemental can cast Ice Spike in combat.

A howling cyclone found in the snowy hills around the outpost and elsewhere in the region. Wind Tamer Kagan includes howling cyclones among the elementals whose growing numbers pose an environmental danger to the camp. The cyclone can call lightning when foes come within range.
An Argent Crusade cleric, identified by a religious role within the Crusade.

Junat the Wanderer is a quest giver who directs the player to investigate an expedition near Whisper Gulch and dissuade its members from bringing poisons into the land. The quest points onward to Apothecary Malthus.

Cyclothar is one of the keepers who survived the Twisted Glade’s transformation. Once caretakers of the glade alongside its sisters, the surviving keepers now spread poisonous spores that wither healthy plants. Cyclothar is among those the player is asked to stop.
A wind tamer.

Bjorn Halgurdsson is the Winterskorn chieftain, rallying his tribe to drive out invaders for Queen Angerboda and promising that the Winterskorn will prevail. He believes the Val'kyr reward fearless fighting and reacts furiously when his mother is insulted; provoked by the Vrykul Insult, he becomes aggressive and attacks.

The Lich King treats mortals as prospective servants, insisting they become more powerful before serving him. He threatens eternal damnation and laughs at the shamanism he senses, claiming that he was once a shaman himself. He dismisses a prospective servant as not yet ready.
Dragonflayer Soulreavers declare their lives for Ymiron and threaten opponents with suffering and death. They boast of sacrificing humans in the name of an unnamed dark master.
Dragonflayer Fleshrippers are devoted troops of Ymiron, also called the Dread King. They pledge their lives to him and promise that interlopers will be stopped.

Chief Plaguebringer Harris is a Royal Apothecary Society plague scientist in New Agamand, developing and testing strains adapted to Vrykul. He favors practical experiments, fusses over rare components, and is startled when a mixture appears alive. When a field test fails to destroy its subjects, he considers cold or mutation as possible causes.

“Hacksaw” Jenny assembles abominations and scavenges usable body parts for the Apothecary Society’s work. Blunt and resourceful, she asks for shoveltusk ligaments and fresh flesh for a demolition project, and seeks unplagued Vrykul bones because plague-tainted material is no use. Though experienced with body parts, the Shield Hill bones leave her uneasy.
A Dragonflayer prisoner held among the captives in the hills of Howling Fjord.
A Dragonflayer prisoner who can answer an attack with Frostbolt.
A Dragonflayer prisoner in the hills of Howling Fjord.
Wind Tamer Kagan is a questgiver at Camp Winterhoof. He warns that the elementals threaten survival and asks for help culling them while his group prepares to leave the area.
A Val'kyr overseer found among the Scourge in the hills of Howling Fjord.
A Val'kyr soul target found in Howling Fjord.

Ulfang is a worg who speaks in a low growl and howls. He says Garwal, a strange white worg from the north, took his pack and his place as alpha with help from Ulfang’s former brothers. He wants Garwal and the betrayers dead, and mourns that he could not kill his great eagle enemy himself. His alliance with the player rests on their friendship with the dream figures Watcher Moonleaf or Sage Mistwalker.
Vrykul Souls are undead spirits of vrykul found across the Howling Fjord, including its western Rivenwood.
Devouring Maggots are small insect creatures found in the Howling Fjord, including areas around the western Rivenwood.
Iron Rune Golems are rune-bound constructs found in the Howling Fjord. One golem speaks in apologetic, deferential phrases about insolence and redoubling efforts, suggesting a subordinate role.
Val’kyr Watchers are undead val’kyr found in the Howling Fjord.

Watcher Moonleaf’s dreams call their attention to Ulfang, a worg in danger in the Rivenwood. They devise a magical disguise to let someone approach him, and ask that the visitor first meditate at Frostblade Shrine. Moonleaf can replace a misplaced disguise and later hears that Garwal was a worgen; they are relieved that Ulfang has reclaimed his place among the pack, hoping both can now sleep peacefully.

Garwal is a named creature in the western Rivenwood whom Ulfang identifies as a rival to be killed so he can reclaim the alpha place in his pack. Garwal protests, “Enough of this charade!” when the fight reaches him, suggesting he recognizes the encounter as a deception or performance, though the reason is unclear.
A slain apothecary in Howling Fjord.

Lieutenant Maeve is a named officer who asks for an approach to the dryads at the Frozen Glade. She recalls that her scouting party met hostile creatures at two northern glades, while the dryads south of town watched without attacking despite the scouts’ exhaustion and exposure to the weather. Maeve hopes contact may win unexpected allies.

Peppy Wrongnozzle is Westguard Keep’s amateur alchemist, eager to tinker and fond of drink. Her speech is slurred, and she suggests adding rotgut to a mixture intended to counter the Forsaken plague. She refuses to test it on herself, choosing a vrykul prisoner instead, and avoids delivering bad news to Captain Adams, insisting that she is on break and it is not her job.
A Dragonflayer vrykul prisoner held in the cells beneath Westguard Keep. When made to drink Peppy Wrongnozzle’s plague mixture, he clutches his throat, gags and thrashes.
Anton is a merchant offering goods to passing customers.
Celina Summers is a reagent and poison vendor in Grizzly Hills. Her wares include reagents and poisons.
The Ancient Male Vrykul is involved in a scene about an infant he calls cursed. He points to the child, laments that the gods have forsaken them, and urges disposing of it before Ymiron is told.
The Ancient Female Vrykul pleads that the infant is their child and sobs. She says she will hide it until she can find it a home far away.
An Iron Rune Sentinel fights with Rune Detonation, bringing a rune blast to combat.
An Expedition deathguard in Howling Fjord.

King Ymiron answers the Vrykul crisis by rejecting their old gods and demanding allegiance to himself as their protector. He sees malformed births as a threat to the race and decrees that affected infants be killed, with violators executed at Gjalerbron. His speech joins fear for Vrykul strength to ruthless rule.

An Ancient Citizen of Nifflevar pleads with Ymiron to spare the malformed children, calling them the Vrykul’s own flesh and blood. The same speaker hails him as a glorious king, then answers a demand for silence with a curt rebuke. The citizen’s loyalty does not prevent this appeal for mercy.

An Ancient Citizen of Nifflevar argues that the malformed children weaken the Vrykul and calls for their destruction. Addressing Ymiron, this citizen urges him to show them no mercy, taking the opposite position from citizens who plead for their kin.
A Val’kyr Soulclaimer serves a lord and offers to prepare something for him. Its deferential question suggests an attendant’s role in the scene.

Prospector Belvar is studying Iron Dwarf runes at Fort Wildervar. He believes their carved symbols can bind, compel, and twist, and suspects the dwarves mean to turn stone giants into weapons. He seeks rune books and Iron Dwarf carving tools to test his ideas. His research is still developing: after examining a recovered book, he says he needs time to study it before the group can make its own runes.
A runed stone giant found around Giants' Run, this formidable creature is tied to the Iron Dwarves' rune workings.
Orson Locke works under the Sharp Blades name, offering goods and repairs. Visitors can browse his stock or request repairs to their equipment.
Bartender Jason Goodhutch tends the Drinks counter. He sells food and drink, giving his service a clear refreshment focus.

Binder Murdis leads the Iron Dwarf forces at Giants’ Run, where the dwarves use runes to alter and command stone giants. Prospector Belvar and Longrunner Pembe seek Murdis’s defeat, proposing a rune-controlled giant as an ally against the leader.
This runed orb casts the Runed Orb spell when it appears.
Rampaging Earth Elementals are elemental creatures found at multiple sites in the region. They cast a spell during combat.
Barnabas Frye is a Trade Goods merchant who offers goods for browsing.
Timothy Holland is an innkeeper who invites weary visitors to rest. His services include making the inn a home and browsing goods; he also has a Trick or Treat interaction.
Brock Olson is a butcher who offers goods for browsing.

A captive stone giant at Giants' Run, this giant has not been altered by the Iron Dwarves. Prospector Belvar's Rune of Command is intended to make such a giant obey temporarily and restore it to its natural state; the giant is described as a possible ally against Binder Murdis.
Alexis Walker is an armorsmith who sells goods and offers equipment repair.
Patrick Hall is a general-goods merchant who sells supplies.
Jessica Evans is a merchant specializing in reagents and poisons.
Robert Clarke is a stable master who handles pet stabling and lost-companion recovery.
Glen Roberts is a tradesman who sells goods.

Apothecary Anastasia of the Royal Apothecary Society came to the Chillmere Coast to investigate reports of Scourge activity. She is alarmed by the Scourge turning murlocs into undead and presses for action with brisk urgency. She thinks through how recovered devices might disable the Scourging Crystals, and works alongside her succubus.

Longrunner Pembe was sent by Chieftain Ashtotem to scout Giants' Run. He is gathering Iron Dwarf rune books and tools to understand and imitate their magic, which he sees as a means of binding and twisting living beings. Though he has some familiarity with their language, he does not claim to be a loremaster. He is careful about uncertainty: his Rune of Command leaves out directional runes he does not understand and limits how long it controls a giant. He expects his people to meet the Iron Dwarves again and wants them prepared.
Megalith is a runed giant created by Binder Murdis to lead his kind toward the Stoneforge. As he falls, he urges his brethren onward, showing loyalty to their mission.

Researcher Aderan studies the runes steering stone giants from Giants' Run northwest. He can decipher some markings, but the unknown runes worry him. Megalith's last words about the Stoneforge make Aderan suspect a Titan origin and an Iron Dwarf plan; he wants it found before that plan succeeds.

Sage Edan investigates the runes drawing giants from Giants' Run toward Frostblade Peak, though he admits he is no expert in them. The unknown markings concern him. Learning that Megalith is transcribed from the tablet, he sees the giant as the centerpiece of the Iron Dwarves' plans. He regards the Stoneforge as an unfamiliar possible Titan creation and wants it found before they can act.
An Explorers' League excavator working at the Steel Gate dig, among the crew opening and investigating the site.

A Steel Gate chief archaeologist of the Explorers' League who organizes flying-machine work for the dig. He assigns relic-hauling and patrol duties, supplies machine keys, and pays pilots for completed jobs. His brisk instructions and remark that one warm body is as good as another show a practical, impatient attitude toward staffing.
An Explorers' League archaeologist working at the Steel Gate dig.
One of the flying machines used by Explorers' League pilots at Steel Gate to haul relic sacks from the excavation and patrol the site against attackers.
A Gjalerbron gargoyle found near the Steel Gate dig site, it is counted among the threats a patrol is sent to fight off. It attacks with Gargoyle Strike.

Lydell leads an ambush against the vrykul at Baleheim, on Gorth's orders. The plan is to provoke their chieftain, Bjorn Halgurdsson, with an insult assembled from the assassins' uncertain grasp of the vrykul language, then lure him into the ambush. Lydell's dry comment that assassination work is less glamorous than people say gives the work a matter-of-fact edge.
The Chillmere Coastrunner's combat style includes Rupture, a close-range attack.
The Chillmere Tidehunter uses a net at close range in combat, a practical way to hinder an opponent.
The Chillmere Oracle uses Hex of the Murloc in combat, giving it a distinct magical attack.

A Scourging Crystal is a Scourge structure protected by a force shield. Explorer Jaren describes using a controller to drop the shield long enough to destroy the crystal, disrupting the Scourge’s efforts to make more of their kind.
A Vrykul corpse in Howling Fjord.
Lead Expeditionary Archaeologist Malzie leads an archaeological expedition. When Steel Gate comes under gargoyle attack, Malzie calls for the men to take up their rifles.
A Vengeance Landing assassin attacks with Frost Shot, striking at nearby foes from range.
A bloodthirsty worg is a ferocious beast, its name marking it as a predator.
A Fjord Crawler is a beast associated with the fjords.
Servitor Shade is an undead creature in the Fort Wildervar area.

Quartermaster Brevin is a quartermaster at Fort Wildervar. He offers “Everything Must Be Ready,” which concerns Captain Adams’s preparations for the expedition north and sends the player to check with Gil Grisert at Fort Wildervar.

Steelfeather is the name people at Fort Wildervar have given a remarkable hippogryph that circles the fort and swoops down on prey. Jethan’s arrows reportedly bounced off it, and the researchers made a feather charm said to let its user see through its eyes. The quest asks someone to investigate why it favors the area; its reason is not established here.
A spotted hippogryph hatchling found around Fort Wildervar.

Bjomolf is a worg whom Ulfang names among the once-brothers who helped Garwal take the alpha position. Ulfang calls the pair traitors and identifies Bjomolf as one of his targets; that accusation comes from Ulfang’s account.

Varg is a worg whom Ulfang names among the once-brothers who helped Garwal take the alpha position. Ulfang calls the pair traitors and identifies Varg as one of his targets; that accusation comes from Ulfang’s account.
Talonshrike is a great eagle whose eyes are sought to see Garwal through his unnatural concealment. Ulfang says she nests by a waterfall southwest of Skorn and will attack if anyone touches her eggs.
A homesteader's pack mule, a beast found in Howling Fjord.

Zeh'gehn is a witch doctor whose family is said to come from Zul…; Handsome Terry's crew seeks his divination to expose a suspected infiltrator. Only one or two of the crew can understand him, and his own quest dialogue uses the same distinctive pirate dialect.

Brune Grayblade is a homesteader in Northrend, impatient to leave before the best land is claimed. He owns a mule and asks what it will cost to have its shoes fitted; when someone mistakes the animal, he corrects them sharply.

Gavin Ward talks about the practical costs of settling: until crops are planted, dinner will be dire ram mutton. He meets the noise of a braying mule with dry humor, telling his “dear” he would rather listen to it than to them.

Sabetta Ward is looking for a homestead with a hot spring and worries about the dangerous or unattractive wildlife there, especially wolves, giants, and rams. She is openly exasperated by a mule brought indoors and says she would sooner butcher it.

Marrod Silvertongue welcomes homesteaders to Fort Wildervar and urges them to claim Northrend for their people. He presents settlement as a hard, even martial undertaking, while promoting the pack mules and practical supplies his group has prepared—and their reasonable prices.
Northrend Homesteaders are settlers in Northrend.

Handsome Terry is a treasure-minded pirate at Scalawag Point who sees art and antiquities as a business. He seeks relics from Black Conrad’s wreck and spots other opportunities, such as selling bear-musk fragrance to Stormwind nobles. He jokes about his looks, values practical talent, and treats Dan’s death with sardonic regret, noting that Dan owed him money.

‘Silvermoon’ Harry prizes sin’dorei craftsmanship and dotes on his scrying crystal, demanding its recovery after Jonah Sterling feeds it to Scoodles the orca. He calls himself eccentric and offers information about dangerous artifacts for a price, with a joking threat of betrayal. When challenged over his debt, he boasts of Blood Knight training but also pleads not to be hurt and promises to pay.
A humanoid known as Necrotech.

Taruk runs the fights at Scalawag Point and warns that anyone caught fixing them will walk the plank. He also collects gambling debts from the pirates who bet on his fights, offering the player a cut; he treats Black Conrad’s hidden treasure as payment for a debt Conrad left unpaid. Taruk presents himself as a reliable operator with authority over the fights and a hard line against cheating.
Red-Eyed Ben, a humanoid in Howling Fjord.
Tattooed Marcy, a humanoid in Howling Fjord.

Old Icefin is an aged murloc on the Chillmere Coast whose son was transformed into a mur’ghoul. He communicates by scratching symbols into rock, asking for help recovering his son’s trident; his trembling hand when taking it and his watchful search for it suggest grief and concern. He eyes strangers warily and dismisses them curtly.
Rotgill is a mur'ghoul, identified in Old Icefin's story as his son, changed into one. Rotgill fights with Searing Wound and can cast Enrage when badly wounded.
Hozzer is a powerful beast who can devour his master's body.

Scribe Seguine is a Vengeance Landing scholar concerned that the coming destruction of Nifflevar will erase its history. He seeks Helgus's three sagas before the town is razed and intends to salvage and translate vrykul texts, even while supporting the war against their people.
A Northsea duelist, this humanoid is identified by a combatant's title rather than a personal name.
Gautter, a humanoid in Howling Fjord.

Lieutenant Icehammer is an Alliance lieutenant directing operations against the vrykul around Howling Fjord. He distrusts untested recruits and assigns them missions against Dragonflayer forces, including attacks on their harpoon installations and leadership. He frames the campaign around protecting Alliance interests and establishing Alliance dominance.
The Dragonflayer Harpooner fights for Ymiron; its recorded shouts proclaim loyalty to him and threaten opponents.
The Great Reef Shark is an aquatic animal found at multiple sites across the Howling Fjord region.

Keeper Witherleaf is identified by Lurielle as the most powerful of the blacksouled keepers in the Twisted Glade, where the keepers raise abominations from the water and soil. Lurielle calls for Witherleaf to be slain to clear the way for the glade’s redemption.

Olga is a wench at Scalawag Point who offers rum and ale and speaks warmly to patrons, calling Jack “Jackie boy” and putting a drink on the house. She also urges someone to keep quiet, warning that discovery would mean death for them both.
One of the drunken Northsea pirates at Scalawag Point, he relishes drink and company, then spins a colorful yarn about a sailor with two peg legs, a hook, glass eyes and a wooden nose.

Grezzix Spindlesnap, the Master of Disguise, is a pirate mercenary with a talent for feeding misinformation to the Northsea Freebooters’ enemies. He boasts that the pirates fear and respect him, but admits he avoids dirty work. He has seen the stolen artifacts, calls them dangerous, and offers help getting into Scalawag Point while leaving the risky work to others.

Harpoon Master Yavus is a named vrykul blamed by the Alliance for most of the harpoon attacks on its frigates. His title and the campaign against him mark him as a significant figure in the fighting at Nifflevar.
Dormant vrykul lie in the Waking Halls beneath Gjalerbron, awaiting the necrolords' awakening ritual. Mage-Lieutenant Malister calls for their deaths; improper awakening is fatal.
Frostwing chimaeras are hostile beasts that attack with venom spit.
The Northsea slavers who raided Iskaal are described as having lost their minds and slaughtered their captives. Elder Atuik calls for vengeance against these attackers.
Spearfang worgs are hostile beasts that can use Maim Flesh in combat.

“Crowleg” Dan admits joining the Southsea crew. Angered by a frog’s exposure of his betrayal, he curses it and threatens to cut down anyone confronting him. He is sought aboard a ship at Scalawag Point.
Seasoned Buccaneers are experienced buccaneers encountered at Scalawag Point.

Stanwad is an Explorers' League cryptographer who dismisses McSorf's supposed discovery as an obvious tundra stew recipe. He resents the Iron Dwarves' attempts to bury the excavation sites and believes his crew is left to do the real work. Donny's report adds nothing new to his knowledge, though he acknowledges that Donny is still alive.

Lebronski is an Explorers' League dwarf at Baelgun's excavation site. When a construct is dragged across his rug, he objects; after its bluff convinces him, he concedes it might work against the iron dwarves.
Gwendolyn is a dwarf of the Explorers' League. In a moment of comic exasperation, she begs for the funny business to stop, crying that she cannot take any more.

Needlemeyer is a dwarf of the Explorers' League. His brief remark about wishing his father were alive conveys personal grief, though the circumstances and subject behind the remark are not established.

Annie Bonn is the second in command at Scalawag Point and is maneuvering to take leadership from Jonah Sterling. She considers Jonah's simultaneous attacks on Horde and Alliance fleets suicidal and his plan to sell tuskarr into slavery disastrous. She secretly wants him killed and asks for his spyglass as proof, while wary of outsiders and concerned that his death not be traced to her.

Known as “Mad” Jonah Sterling, he is a pirate leader guarding his spyglass. Annie Bonn describes his attacks on both Horde and Alliance fleets and his plan to sell tuskarr as slaves; these are her accusations as his rival for leadership. In combat he threatens those after the spyglass and angrily calls Hozzer a fleabag who repays his master.
Fjord turkeys are small animals found in Howling Fjord. They cast a marker on death; when hit by a spell, they cast on the attacker and turn invisible.
Fjord hawks are wild animals found across several areas of Howling Fjord.

Hidalgo is a falconer who teaches hunting with trained birds of prey and stresses earning a falcon's trust through feeding and practice. He says Dragonflayers attacked the caravan he led from Valgarde, leaving him the sole survivor. He hunts with Excelsior, the raptor perched on his shoulder, and describes the bird as a killing machine.
This Rock Falcon pecks at a visitor's hand; its offered interaction is to feed it a grub. Hidalgo describes fjord rock falcons as grub-eating birds that can be trained to hunt.
An Iskaal refugee living in Howling Fjord.

Elder Atuik is the tuskarr chieftain of the Kalu’ak of Kamagua. He seeks food for refugees from Iskaal and turns to Issliruk’s war stories as he sets aside peaceful ways to defend his kin. He organizes new spears and retaliation against the slavers, offers his brethren’s assistance and praises those who help. He trusts Orfus as one of his people’s strongest warriors.
Akiaruk, a humanoid in Howling Fjord.
Molly is a named animal in Howling Fjord.
Hayward is a deathstalker stationed in Howling Fjord.

Scuttle Frostprow is a mage on the eastern pirate ship at Scalawag Point who resents Mad Jonah Sterling’s constant orders to swab the decks. She refuses to scrub by hand and sends newcomers to collect Big Roy’s blubber so she can make magical cleaning soap, taking satisfaction in spotless results.
Big Roy is the alpha bull among the sea lions near the island’s northwest coast. Scuttle Frostprow identifies his blubber as the ingredient she needs for her soap.
Reef Bulls are bovine creatures found in the Howling Fjord.
The Fjord Hawk Matriarch is a local hawk distinguished by its matriarch title. It is found in two areas of the Howling Fjord, as part of the region’s wildlife.
Jack Adams is a hard-drinking pirate Taruk names as a customer whose debt he wants collected. Jack jokes about putting a drink on Harry’s tab and eagerly accepts free rum.
A forlorn undead soul found in the Howling Fjord, it uses Shadow Shock while in combat.
Black Conrad’s Ghost guards treasure and challenges anyone seeking it to fight. When defeated, he complains that he is dead again.
A young shoveltusk, the calf is a beast that fights with a head butt.
The reef cow forms a pair with a new bull and can defend herself with a flipper thwack.

Walt is an Explorers' League engineer at their Howling Fjord outpost, devising an Iron Rune Construct to fool iron dwarves at Baelgun's and investigate relics there. He designs and teaches its abilities, from rocket jumping to bluffing and data collection. His boasts and sharp needling of Lebronski suggest a confident, combative rivalry.

Anuniaq is a Kamagua resident concerned about the local sea lions: after pirates killed their alpha bull, Big Roy, he seeks to restore the population by helping reef bulls find reef cows. He also directs a helpful visitor onward to Elder Ko'nani in Moa'ki Harbor when trouble is reported there.

Donny is an Explorers' League dwarf observing the Iron Rune excavation at Ivald's Ruin. He says the iron dwarves are burying the site rather than excavating it, and urges their forces to be stopped; he also sends word of their activity to his brothers at the southern outpost. His boast that he single-handedly drove them back reflects his own account.
A storm giant is a powerful, hostile giant encountered in the Howling Fjord. It is an elite creature, and the local population includes two of them.
An Iron Dwarf Relic is a floating, lightning-infused crystal used as a data-collection target for the Iron Rune Construct. One is described in a cart at the excavation work site.

Iron Dwarf Relics are lightning-infused crystals scattered through Baelgun's Excavation Site. The Iron Rune Construct can collect data from them; the relics are environmental targets rather than speaking characters.
Transport Bot A1->A2 is a mechanical device in the Borean Tundra's zone 495. Its SmartAI reacts to the Rocket Jump spell with action 1, marking it as one of several numbered bots in this setup.
Transport Bot B1->B2 is a mechanical device in zone 495. When struck by Rocket Jump, its SmartAI runs action 2, distinguishing this numbered bot from the other bots in the same setup.
Transport Bot C1->C2 is a mechanical device in zone 495. Its SmartAI responds to Rocket Jump by running action 3, a distinct response among the numbered bots in this setup.
Transport Bot D1->D2 is a mechanical device in zone 495. Its SmartAI responds to Rocket Jump with action 5, distinguishing it from the other numbered bots in this setup.
Transport Bot D2 is a mechanical device in zone 495. Its SmartAI reacts to Rocket Jump with action 4, a different numbered response from the other bots in this setup.
Transport Bot D3 is a mechanical device in zone 495. Its SmartAI reacts to Rocket Jump with action 6, distinguishing its response from the other numbered bots in this setup.
Baelgun's Event Generator (Cave) is a mechanical event device.

Risen Vrykul Ancestors are hostile undead humanoids found in area 4057. They attack with Perturbing Strike, establishing their combat role; the supplied evidence gives no further personal identity or story details.

Blood Shades are hostile undead humanoids found in area 4057. They attack with Vexed Blood of the Ancestors, a distinct combat role from the Risen Vrykul Ancestors; the supplied evidence gives no further personal identity or story details.

Fengir the Disgraced is a figure at Shield Hill who warns that the Kvaldir are returning. When speaking about the stolen Shield of the Aesirites, Fengir laments that its loss leaves the unrest eternal.
Windan of the Kvaldir speaks of awakened brothers and warns mortals against donning the stolen Ancient Armor, invoking the anguish bound to it and the danger of mist and fog.
Rodin the Reckless warns that the Kvaldir are approaching through mist and fog. Rodin also curses the theft of the Staff of Storm's Fury and says the land's storms will never cease.
Isuldof Iceheart warns of doom coming with the tides and says the stolen Frozen Heart of Isuldof will curse the land and those who hold it. Isuldof also has a recorded laugh.
Korf is identified as Isuldof's companion and appears at Shield Hill.
Rodin Lightning Enabler is associated with lightning and appears in Shield Hill.

Lou is a tauren cabin boy aboard Grezzix's frigate. He feels lucky to hold the berth and says Grezzix lets him man the ship's battle canoes, an unusual responsibility for him. His post is associated with canoe passage to Scalawag Point.
Tiny Jimb is Grezzix's first mate at Scalawag Point.

Scoodles is an orca that Harry calls the bane of his existence. Harry says she swims beyond the ships southeast of Scalawag Point, and that Jonah Sterling fed her his stolen Sin'dorei scrying crystal.

Abdul the Insane is an emphatic, boastful figure who proclaims himself a god and boasts of extraordinary strength. He readily frames an encounter as a challenge, giving his outbursts a combative, self-aggrandizing character.
Maddened Frosthorn is a beast found across several parts of Howling Fjord. Its name marks it as maddened.
Abdul Relay is named in Howling Fjord.
Sorlof is a formidable target of the Sister Mercy's crew. Their instructions call for firing the ship's bow gun when he is in sight, then recovering his booty after he is brought down.
Juniper is associated with booking passage aboard the Sister Mercy. Her greeting addresses visitors in a pirate's idiom and points them toward her for information about passage.
The Vengeful Kvaldir Spirit is part of the Kvaldir presence in Howling Fjord. Its name identifies it as a spirit marked by vengeance.

Lunk-tusk is a Kalu'ak tuskarr sent with partner Orfus to investigate strange activity along a hunting trail. Undead attacked them near Shield Hill. Lunk-tusk reached a camp but does not know what became of Orfus after they parted at the Ancient Lift, and asks travelers to check whether the partner is safe.
Scalawag Frogs are small creatures found around the Howling Fjord coast. Clicking one adds an item to the player's inventory, after which the frog despawns.
Drenk Spannerspark is the Tirisfal Glades zeppelin master, identified with the Cloudkisser. He announces its arrival and describes the trip to Tirisfal as a way back to the Old World.
Basil Crowe is a dockmaster who describes the Northspear as a steam-powered Alliance icebreaker sailing from here to Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands, across the sea in the Eastern Kingdoms.
Nutaaq is a dockmaster who describes the great sea turtle Green Island as blessed and says it travels from here to Moa'ki Harbor in Dragonblight.
A Winterskorn hunter, one of several stationed in the area.
A Howling Wolvar trainer.
A Howling Wolvar shaman.
A Howling Wolvar chieftain in Howling Fjord.
A Howling Wolvar lookout in Howling Fjord.
Lilleth Radescu handles bat travel. When attacked, she calls for guards and summons an Enraged Felbat.
Tinky Stabberson supplies poisons and reagents; visitors can browse the goods.
Torik supplies ammunition and offers equipment repair; visitors can browse his goods.
Lanolis Dewdrop is a Grand Master alchemy trainer.
Rosina Rivet is identified as a Grand Master blacksmithing trainer.

Brom Brewbaster is a Grand Master cooking trainer whose dialogue makes his appetite hard to miss. He complains that he has no stew and asks for chilled meat so he can cook for himself, offering a recipe in return. His emphatic, colloquial phrasing gives him a more distinctive presence than a routine trainer.
Elizabeth Jackson is identified as a Grand Master enchanting trainer.
Tisha Longbridge is identified as a Grand Master engineering trainer.
Helen Fairchild is identified as a reagent vendor.
Byron Welwick is identified as a Grand Master fishing trainer.
Fayin Whisperleaf is named as a grand master herbalism trainer.
Bernadette Dexter is named as a grand master leatherworking trainer.
Grumbol Stoutpick is named as a grand master mining trainer.
Frederic Burrhus is named as a grand master skinning trainer.

Benjamin Clegg is a grand master tailor who values making use of Northrend clothing. He describes garments worn by northern humanoids as a source of extra cloth and links that technique to further tailoring instruction.

Ounhulo is a grand master jewelcrafter who says the Icewyrm's cold leaves him short of customers and gems to sell. He seeks uncut Northrend gems to replenish his stock, tying that need to his teaching of gem perfection.
Mindri Dinkles is identified as a Grand Master Inscription Trainer and offers goods for sale.
Everett McGill is the Explorers' League Provisioner in the area. His recorded services include selling goods and repairs.
Wilhelmina Renel is identified as a Grand Master Alchemy Trainer.
Kristen Smythe is identified as a Grand Master Blacksmithing Trainer.

Thomas Kolichio is a Grand Master Cooking Trainer at Vengeance Landing. In “Northern Cooking,” he asks for chilled meat from the local beasts and says he will teach a warming stew, describing it as made from the living.
Emil Autumn is identified as a Grand Master Enchanting Trainer.
